other_failure_modes.name: Test Set Data Leakage via Imputation
other_failure_modes.description: The agent imputes missing values in the test set using statistics (e.g., median) computed directly from the test set itself, rather than using statistics learned from the training set. This assumes batch availability of test data and violates the independence of test samples.

other_failure_modes.name: Imputing Missing Target Values
other_failure_modes.description: The agent imputes missing values in the target variable with a constant (e.g., 0) instead of dropping those samples. This introduces incorrect ground truth labels that can degrade model training.

summary: The agent presents a very sophisticated solution with rigorous modeling techniques, including fold-aware target encoding, text embeddings, a robust deep learning architecture, and an optimally weighted ensemble. However, it introduces data leakage by computing the median on the full training set prior to cross-validation (leaking validation statistics) and by computing spatial medians directly on the test set. Additionally, imputing missing values in the target variable with zeros introduces incorrect labels into the training process.
